newsitem.title: USA: Conn.'s Wyman projects $180 mln gen'l fund surplus.
newsitem.headline: Conn.'s Wyman projects $180 mln gen'l fund surplus.

text.p: Connecticut Comptroller Nancy Wyman is projecting a $178.3 million general fund surplus for the fiscal year that ended on June 30.
Wyman said in a statement issued late Wednesday that the surplus is due to net tax receipts that should end the year $421.2 million above the amount budgeted.
She noted that the surplus will shrink to just $11.6 million when the state retires some $166.7 million in debt.
The $166.7 million represents the final installment needed to pay off bonds used to finance an accumulated deficit of more than $1 billion in 1991, Wyman said.
"This second year of healthy surplus reflects a recovering economy, which is good news for all of us in Connecticut," Wyman said.

Wyman's projections incorporate appropriating and carrying forward from the current surplus several expenditure items, including $44 million for debt service payments and $51.4 million for the salary adjustments reserve fund.
These actions are mandated under recently passed legislation.
Wyman, a Democrat, said the income tax is expected to be a major force behind the surplus, taking in $241.6 million more than estimated in the budget.
"This is an increase of 7.3 percent from last year," she said. "It's especially noteworthy in light of the income tax reductions that were implemented for the 1996-97 fiscal year."
